text:
maria: quick heads-up — saw a weird perf regression on H100 with the paged-flash variant. seq_len=8192, bsz=2, token-latency jumped ~1.8x compared to last week. posting raw numbers below.

lucas: ouch. command you ran? model, quant, commit?

maria: commit 9f2a3d7 (kernel-selector change), model llama-2-70b, 4-bit q4f16, run: `./bench_run --device h100 --model llama-2-70b --seq 8192 --bs 2 --kernel paged_flash_v3 --kv-cache on`

perf-bot: auto-bench summary for thread 1718001234:
- h100 (paged_flash_v3): 85 tokens/s, p50 token-latency 11.8ms, mem high-water 42GB
- a100 (paged_flash_v3): 132 tokens/s, p50 token-latency 7.6ms, mem 40GB
- l40s (paged_flash_v3): 95 tokens/s, p50 10.2ms, mem 38GB
Reference (last stable run, commit 7a1b2c4):
- h100: 153 tokens/s, p50 6.5ms

nora: interesting — perf-bot shows mem HWM spiked on H100 only. my hunch: KV cache allocator falling back to host pages and causing memcpy storms. I pulled the trace from perf tools:
```
[kernel] alloc_pages_order: order=3 returned 0 pages, fallback to host pinned
memcpy_h2d: 1.2s total across iteration window
```

kai: can you re-run with `REDWOOD_KERNEL_HINTS=prefer_small_kv` and `FLASH_PREFETCH=0`? also try `--split-streams=2` flag from the selector PR — we saw similar convoys on H100 before.

maria: re-ran with those hints + split-streams=2. new numbers: h100: 140 tokens/s, p50 6.9ms, mem 39GB. so that helps a lot. looks like the selector picked a hotpath that overwhelms H100 page allocator.

lucas: great repro. can you capture `nvprof` timeline + the runtime selector logs? also start with `KERNEL_SELECTOR_DEBUG=1` so we get the decision trace.

maria: pasted selector trace snippet:
```
[selector] seq=8192 bsz=2 candidate=[paged_flash_v3, fused_flash_v1]
score[paged_flash_v3]=0.62 (est_latency 6.2ms, est_mem 41GB)
score[fused_flash_v1]=0.55 (est_latency 5.9ms, est_mem 45GB)
chosen=paged_flash_v3 -> apply split_streams=1
```

nora: aha — estimator underpredicted mem pressure, so the runtime chose paged_flash_v3 without split_streams. estimator models need tuning for >6k sequences on H100. the fallback host pinning is the main culprit.

lucas: can we add a quick guard: if est_mem > gpu_mem * 0.85 then force split_streams>=2 or pick fused variant? low-risk hotfix.

maria: I created a tiny canary patch and ran it: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2029
results with canary selector: h100 148 tokens/s, p50 6.6ms, mem 40GB. seems stable across 3 runs.

kai: nice. let's also add an eval job in the perf dashboard for seq_len sweep [2048,4096,8192,12288] x bsz [1,2,4] on h100/a100/l40s so we can catch regressions earlier. I'll add the dashboard tile.

maria: will kick off bisect between 7a1b2c4..9f2a3d7 to find the exact commit that changed estimator behavior. posting bisect script for reviewers:
```
#!/bin/bash
git bisect start 9f2a3d7 7a1b2c4
git bisect run ./bench_run --device h100 --model llama-2-70b --seq 8192 --bs 2 --kernel paged_flash_v3 --kv-cache on --quiet
```

lucas: ping me when bisect finds a candidate commit. also tag infra for a short H100 maintenance window if we need to re-run long sweeps.

perf-bot: scheduled perf-sweep: eng-runtime/h100-seq-bsz-sweep queued by kai (ETA 2h).

maria: thanks all — bisect in progress. if anyone sees similar anomalies on A100/L40s please paste numbers here. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
